answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce, slashable stake before it may post bids or validate work. A trellis of repeated, time-separated tasks then builds a reputation record, while an anchor of collateral remains at risk if an agent double-signs or colludes. Sybils cannot cheaply multiply influence: each needs more capital, and coordinated fraud can forfeit it. The reef is that stake alone cannot prove one human or stop wealthy attackers, so limits and audits still matter.
